messages:
olivia: FYI triage — upstream security disclosures today for a few Go deps we use: net/http path parsing DoS (reported), grpc auth token parsing fix, and a JWT library vuln that affects token validation. Need quick classification + patch plan.

sarthak: link to advisories?

olivia: https://security.example/cve-2026-nethttp-dos (mock link) and https://security.example/cve-2026-grpc-auth and https://security.example/cve-2026-jose. Short notes: net/http requires go 1.20+ patched net patch, grpc pinned to v1.58.1, go-jose needs v2.8.0.

kevin: summary impact on our products: hosted API (low-level reverse proxy) uses net/http directly in router; Dedicated runtime uses grpc heavily between controller <-> runtime; auth service uses go-jose for JWT validation.

maya: marking high for auth service (token validation bug). net/http DoS looks MEDIUM unless we see heavy malformed path traffic.

aaron: can we mitigate with code changes (sanitizers) instead of immediate upstream bump?

sarthak: net/http fix is upstream runtime change; short-term we can add extra request-path length checks in our gateway (fast). For grpc/auth we should prefer library upgrade.

olivia: proposed triage/prioritization: 1) auth service (go-jose v2.8.0) — HIGH, patch immediately + hotfix release. 2) grpc token parsing — HIGH, upgrade to v1.58.1 and add unit tests for token edge cases. 3) net/http DoS — MEDIUM, add gateway mitigations + schedule patch with next Go runtime upgrade.

kevin: agree. Who will own each PR?

maya: I'll take auth service PR and backport to 1.3.x branch. Plan: bump in go.mod, run unit + integration tests, then small canary to staging.

aaron: I'll do grpc bump and add a test for the malformed token case. Will open PR later today.

olivia: For net/http I'll file an ops ticket to add request path length limits in the gateway config and add a runtime upgrade ticket for Go 1.20+ in our infra backlog.

kevin: CI checklist for each PR: 
- update go.mod + go.sum
- run `make test` and `make integration`
- reproducible build smoke (static checks)
- add CHANGELOG entry referencing CVE
- tag release and notify support

maya: draft patch snippet for auth service bump:

```
module github.com/redwood/auth-service

require (
  github.com/square/go-jose v2.8.0 // CVE-2026-jose
)
```

maya: also adding unit test for an edge-case token with empty kid and malformed alg.

aaron: grpc bump command I'll use in PR: `go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.58.1` and then `go mod tidy`.

olivia: rollout plan: patch -> internal canary (5% traffic) for 24h -> increase to 50% if no regressions -> full. For Dedicated customers with reserved pools, schedule maintenance window and notify. For Private installs, send advisory + backport patch notes.

kevin: add observability: enable debug-level auth failure metric and new audit log entry for rejected tokens with reason code. That helps validate fix.

maya: will add AuditLog: JWT_VALIDATION_FAILURE:{reason} with truncated token hash. Need ops signoff for log retention.

olivia: ops signoff needed: @bot-deploy can you queue a canary deployment after PRs land? Also we need KMS note — jwt changes shouldn't affect KMS but double-check signing key rotation logic.

bot-deploy: deploy-bot: acknowledged. Will trigger canary pipeline when the PR is merged and CI passes.

aaron: KMS check: the auth service only validates tokens; signing is done by identity service. I'll coordinate with identity team to ensure no rotation incompatibility.

kevin: timelines?

maya: auth PR by EOD, canary tomorrow morning. Backport PR same day.

aaron: grpc PR by EOD, canary tomorrow afternoon.

olivia: assign severity labels in tracker: auth=P1, grpc= P1, nethttp = P2. Add CVE references and link to this thread.

kevin: one more thing — add dependency pinning policy to our CONTRIBUTING doc: require explicit versions for indirect deps in go.mod when security fixes are required. Saves surprises.

olivia: agreed. I'll open a small RFC to formalize pin/backport rules after immediate fixes.

maya: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/auth-service/pull/472 (draft) — includes tests and CHANGELOG.

kevin: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pull/889 (ops change for path length limit).

aaron: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/mesh/pull/203 (grpc bump).

olivia: thanks folks. After canaries, I'll coordinate support notice and publish advisory. :thumbsup:

kevin: one-liner follow-up — let's also run our vuln scanner across mono-repo to catch any other transitive uses of the vulnerable jwt lib.

maya: done, running now.

bot-deploy: deploy-bot: canary started for auth-service v1.12.1-canary at 1746052000

olivia: closing thread when all PRs merged and canaries clear. Keep updates here.
